## Savory meal-prep pairing

### Easy, reliable Instant Pot lentils
**Rainbow Plant Life — [How to Cook Lentils in the Instant Pot](https://rainbowplantlife.com/how-to-cook-lentils-in-the-instant-pot/)** (4.9/5 from 146 votes)

- **Base:** 1 cup brown, green, French green/Puy, or black beluga lentils; **1¾ cups** water or vegetable broth; **½ tsp kosher salt** and pepper.
- **Method:** combine in the pot, pressure-cook on High **6–8 minutes** for firm/al dente lentils (best for bowls/salads) or **10 minutes** for softer lentils. Let pressure release naturally **10 minutes**, then vent remaining steam.
- **Time:** 2 minutes prep; 32 minutes total as listed.
- **Make-ahead:** refrigerate airtight **5–7 days** or freeze **4–6 months**.
- **Practical note:** this timing specifically excludes red/split lentils, which break down quickly. For your batch lunches, use brown/green/Puy/Beluga so the lentils retain structure.

### Vegetable-forward turkey chili
**Ambitious Kitchen — [The Best Healthy Turkey Chili](https://www.ambitiouskitchen.com/seriously-the-best-healthy-turkey-chili/)**

- **Yield/time:** 6 servings of about **1½ cups**; 10-minute prep, 45-minute cook, **55 minutes total**.
- **Vegetable/plant-forward components:** yellow onion, 3 garlic cloves, red bell pepper, a 28-ounce can of tomatoes, 2 cans kidney beans, and sweet corn. The recipe’s vegetable trio is onion, pepper, and corn; beans and tomatoes add further fiber-rich plant volume.
- **Protein base:** 1 lb extra-lean (99%) ground turkey or chicken.
- **Seasoning:** chili powder, cumin, oregano, cayenne, and salt. The author used mild McCormick chili powder; with a hotter brand, start at **2–3 Tbsp** rather than the listed 4 Tbsp.
- **Method:** sauté onion, garlic, and pepper **5–7 minutes**; brown turkey; bloom spices briefly; add tomatoes, broth, beans, and corn. Bring to a boil, then simmer **30–45 minutes** until thick.
- **Meal-prep storage:** cooled, untopped chili keeps about **1 week** refrigerated or up to **3 months** frozen. Slow-cooker option: reduce broth to **½ cup**, brown turkey/onions first, then cook 3–4 hours High or 6–7 hours Low.
- **Per listed 1½-cup serving:** 336 calories, 31.8 g protein, 17.4 g fiber, and 3.7 g fat.

**Pairing assessment:** These work well in the same week because the lentils are a neutral, sturdy high-fiber base while the chili supplies lean protein, beans, tomatoes, and vegetables. I’d portion lentils separately rather than stirring them into the chili, so the lentils keep their texture and you can alternate lunches—lentil bowls one day, chili the next. If serving together, use a smaller scoop of lentils under the chili, since the chili already contains two cans of kidney beans.

## Feel Good Foodie desserts

- **[Halva](https://feelgoodfoodie.net/recipe/halva/)** — Tahini, sugar, water, rose water, and pistachios. Active prep/cook is 25 minutes, plus 2½ hours resting; syrup must reach **235°F**. Keeps about **1 week** airtight in the refrigerator. It’s make-ahead capable but comparatively technique-sensitive and rich (listed 227 calories and 19 g sugar per ounce).

- **[3-Ingredient Chia Pudding](https://feelgoodfoodie.net/recipe/3-ingredient-chia-pudding/)** — Almond milk (or another milk), chia seeds, and sweetener. Five-minute prep; its preferred ratio is **2 Tbsp chia seeds to ½ cup milk** per snack serving; chill overnight. It keeps up to **5 days** refrigerated and can be frozen up to 1 month. Keep toppings separate until serving.

- **[Pecan Bars](https://feelgoodfoodie.net/recipe/pecan-bars/)** — A four-ingredient shortbread crust with a date-sweetened pecan filling. Bake crust 20 minutes at **350°F**, then filling 30 minutes; cool 2 hours before slicing. Makes 24 bars; refrigerate airtight **4–5 days**, or individually wrap and freeze up to **3 months**.

### My two make-ahead picks
1. **Chia pudding** — the clear everyday choice: minimal hands-on work, easy to portion into jars, holds for the workweek, and is the most aligned with a lighter, healthier prep plan.
2. **Pecan bars** — best second choice because they portion cleanly, refrigerate/freeze very well, and the dates reduce reliance on refined sugar in the filling. Make them when you want a more substantial dessert.

I’d skip halva for this particular prep week—not because it cannot be made ahead, but because it needs candy-temperature precision and is more calorie- and sugar-dense per small serving than the other two options.
